The story is told entirely from the single, close third-person perspective of the ferry operator, Ilse Brandt. While three passengers board the ferry (an older regular, an unfamiliar young woman, and a teenage boy), the narrative only observes their external actions and dialogue through Ilse's eyes without diving into their internal mindsets or providing diverse perspectives. Furthermore, there are no morally ambiguous, objectionable, or truly unlikeable characters whose complex motivations are explored; Ilse is simply stoic and reserved.
